title: Practice 10: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Ну, ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) я.
exercises.why: **пошел** is the past tense (masculine) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». past: он пошёл · она пошла́ · оно пошло́ · они пошли́. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  From Иван Шмелёв, «Солнце мёртвых».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Михаил Салтыков-Щедрин, «Карась-идеалист».

exercises.q: Как же ___ (слетать — to fly there and back)?
exercises.why: **слетает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **слетать** (to fly down (from), to fly away (from)) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. present: я слета́ю · ты слета́ешь · он слета́ет · мы слета́ем · вы слета́ете · они слета́ют. — Wiktionary, «слетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «лететь — летать: perfective полететь · «for a while» полетать · «round trip» слетать.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  From Фёдор Достоевский, «Братья Карамазовы».
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Все бы ___ (поплавать — to swim for a while).
exercises.why: **поплавать** (the infinitive) (to swim for a while, to float for a while) — the perfective of **плавать** meaning «for a while». — Wiktionary, «поплавать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  From Фёдор Решетников, «Подлиповцы».
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Думаешь, не ___ (полезть — to start climbing)?
exercises.why: **полезу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **полезть** (to climb (up, on to), to scramble) — the perfective of **лезть**, «set out». future: я поле́зу · ты поле́зешь · он поле́зет · мы поле́зем · вы поле́зете · они поле́зут. — Wiktionary, «полезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Владимир Короленко, «В дурном обществе».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Как не ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot))?
exercises.why: **пойдёте** is the future tense (2nd person plural) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». future: я пойду́ · ты пойдёшь · он пойдёт · мы пойдём · вы пойдёте · они пойду́т. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  From Максим Горький, «Жизнь ненужного человека».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)
